_meta.purpose: Map measured characteristics → DAW-specific plugin settings. Stock/free first; paid as upgrade. Written before any affiliate relationships.
_meta.status: v0 — stock tiers filled for Logic / Ableton / Pro Tools
_meta.honesty: Recommendations are plausible reconstructions with reasoning, never claimed true chains.

mud.orderNote: Cut mud before boosting presence or air — otherwise you amplify the cloud.
mud.teaching: On finished R&B/rap masters the vocal often sits on a dense low-mid bed (808 + pads). A narrow cut around 250–400 Hz in the vocal region estimate is usually about clarity, not making it thin.

logic.settings: Bell, ~320 Hz, −2 to −3 dB, Q ~1.2. Check at 250 and 400 — pick the one that opens the lyric without hollowing the body.
logic.notes: Stock first. Listen in context of the full mix estimate.

ableton.settings: Bell, ~320 Hz, −2 to −3 dB, Q ~1.2. Solo the band briefly, then set by ear against the 808.

pro_tools.settings: Band 3 or 4 bell, ~320 Hz, −2 to −3 dB, Q ~1.2.

logic.notes: Dynamic EQ if mud only blooms on loud syllables.

ableton.notes: Dynamic EQ if mud only blooms on loud syllables.

pro_tools.notes: Dynamic EQ if mud only blooms on loud syllables.

logic.notes: Upgrade path — not required for this cut.

ableton.notes: Upgrade path — not required for this cut.

pro_tools.notes: Upgrade path — not required for this cut.

sibilance.orderNote: De-ess before brightening. Adding air on an untamed S will scream.
sibilance.teaching: Sibilance on modern rap/R&B is often exaggerated by clipper + limiter chains. Aim for control, not deletion — dead-S vocals sound amateur.

logic.settings: Start around 6–7 kHz, medium range. Threshold so S ducks ~3–6 dB on peaks only.

ableton.gap: Ableton has no dedicated stock de-esser.
ableton.settings: Workaround: EQ Eight dynamic-style — narrow bell 6–7 kHz into Compressor sidechain, or split at 5 kHz with Multiband Dynamics and compress the high band lightly.
ableton.notes: This gap is the product finding — stock users cannot route around it by buying nothing.

pro_tools.settings: HF band ~6–7 kHz; range so peaks pull 3–6 dB.

ableton.notes: Or Tokyo Dawn TDR Nova dynamic band at 6–7 kHz.

logic.notes: Stock DeEsser is enough for v0.

pro_tools.notes: Stock DeEsser is enough for v0.

logic.notes: Finer detection; buy only if stock still lisps or dulls.

ableton.notes: Highest-leverage paid buy for Ableton stock users.

pro_tools.notes: Upgrade if stock dulls the top.

harshness.orderNote: Soften harshness before heavy compression — compressors can glue the bite into the whole performance.
harshness.teaching: Harshness here is often ear-fatigue from presence EQ + saturation, not just 'too much treble.' A wide, shallow cut usually beats a surgical notch.

logic.settings: Wide bell, ~3.2 kHz, −1.5 to −2.5 dB, Q ~0.7–1.0.

ableton.settings: Wide bell, ~3.2 kHz, −1.5 to −2.5 dB, Q ~0.7–1.0.

pro_tools.settings: Wide bell, ~3.2 kHz, −1.5 to −2.5 dB, Q low.

logic.notes: Only if the harshness moves with the performance.

ableton.notes: Dynamic cut if bite only on loud lines.

pro_tools.notes: Dynamic cut if bite only on loud lines.

air.description: Energy above ~8 kHz relative to body
air.orderNote: Air last among EQ moves — after mud, harshness, and de-ess.
air.teaching: Contemporary R&B/rap air is often a gentle shelf plus saturation harmonics, not a huge +6 dB sparkle. Match the measurement with restraint.

logic.settings: High shelf ~10–12 kHz. Elevated air: −1 to −2 dB. Recessed air: +1 to +2.5 dB. Keep Q gentle.
logic.notes: If sibilance was elevated, de-ess first or the shelf will fight you.

ableton.settings: High shelf ~10–12 kHz, ±1 to ±2.5 dB depending on elevated/recessed.

logic.notes: Tiny drive can create air-like harmonics without a shelf.

ableton.notes: Soft mode, drive low — harmonics before EQ shelf.

pro_tools.notes: Prefer mild saturation over aggressive shelves.

dynamics_crest.orderNote: Shape tone before you glue dynamics. Order: EQ/de-ess → compress → limit/clip.
dynamics_crest.teaching: Low crest on modern vocals usually means serial compression (fast then slow) into a clipper or limiter — not one plugin at −20 dB GR. High crest means leave headroom; don't crush to imitate a denser record.

logic.settings: Compressor: ratio 3:1–4:1, attack 8–15 ms, release auto/50–80 ms, 3–5 dB GR. Then Limiter: catch peaks 1–2 dB. For denser targets, add a second Compressor earlier (faster attack, 2–3 dB GR) before the main one.
logic.notes: Logic has no dedicated clipper — soft saturation before the limiter approximates edge.

ableton.settings: Compressor 3:1, attack ~10 ms, ~3–5 dB GR. Glue for bus-like density (soft knee, low GR). Limiter last for peaks. Saturator before Limiter if you want clipper-like density.

pro_tools.settings: Dyn3 ~3:1–4:1, attack 8–15 ms, 3–5 dB GR. Maxim for ceiling. Serial: two Dyn3 stages beat one smashed stage.

logic.notes: Multiband smash is a genre tool; easy to overdo.

ableton.notes: Familiar density tool — start wet/dry low.

logic.notes: Finer timing and true peak control.

ableton.notes: Upgrade when stock timing feels blunt.

pro_tools.notes: Upgrade when stock timing feels blunt.

stereo_width.orderNote: Width last. Widen support (doubles, verb, delays) — keep the lead take centered.
stereo_width.teaching: Wide vocal regions on records usually come from stacked doubles and FX returns, not a stereo widener on the main mono vocal. Narrow images mean respect the center; don't fake width.

logic.settings: Lead: keep mono/center. Width: short stereo delay 60–120 ms low feedback, or subtle Doubler. Verb on a send, not inserted wide on the lead.

ableton.settings: Lead Utility width ~0–20%. Delay return ping-pong subtle. Reverb on send. Avoid Wideners on the main vocal.

pro_tools.plugin: Mod Delay III / D-Verb / Air Stereo Width (if available)
pro_tools.settings: Center the lead. Build width on sends. If using a width plugin, restrict to FX bus.

low_end_mask.description: Sub/bass vs low-mid masking on an instrumental or mix bus
low_end_mask.orderNote: Carve kick vs bass and HPF non-bass groups before bus glue.
low_end_mask.teaching: On modern beds the kick and 808 share the bottom. A narrow carve (often 40–80 Hz or a mid-bass dip) plus mono lows keeps the instrumental clear under a vocal.

logic.settings: HPF non-bass groups ~80–120 Hz. Bell carve where kick and bass fight. Keep master/sub mono.

ableton.settings: Group HPFs on non-bass. Opposite bells on kick vs bass. Utility mono below ~120 Hz on the bus.

pro_tools.settings: HPF non-bass paths. Surgical carve between kick and bass fundamentals.

logic.notes: Dynamic bands help when mud only blooms on hits.

ableton.notes: Dynamic bands help when mud only blooms on hits.

pro_tools.notes: Dynamic bands help when mud only blooms on hits.

bus_glue.description: Mix/instrumental bus compression from crest density
bus_glue.orderNote: Glue after corrective EQ; before aggressive limiting.
bus_glue.teaching: 1–2 dB of SSL-style bus compression is what makes a bed feel finished. Stacking another limiter on an already-dense master just kills transients.

logic.settings: Ratio 2:1–4:1, attack 10–40 ms, ~1–2 dB GR. Mix/parallel if available.

ableton.settings: Soft clip off at first. 2:1–4:1, slow-ish attack, 1–2 dB GR.

pro_tools.settings: 2:1–3:1, attack ~30 ms, gentle GR. Save brickwall for the master.

stereo_image.description: Side/mid balance for instrumental and mix-bus imaging
stereo_image.orderNote: Mono the lows; open width above the low-mids only.
stereo_image.teaching: Finished instrumentals keep sub/bass mono and put width on hats, pads, and FX. A single widener on the whole bus is how mixes fall apart on phones.

logic.settings: Narrow below ~120–180 Hz. Optional width above 5 kHz. Always check mono.

ableton.settings: Bass mono. Width on return tracks more than the master bus.

pro_tools.plugin: Air Stereo Width / Trim + pan law discipline
pro_tools.settings: Keep low end centered. Restrict wideners to FX/buses.

logic.notes: Multiband control when stock feels blunt.
